subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: Should explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec warn and continue without PTY, fail closed, or become supported through sandbox backend PTY where available?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix defines user-visible behavior at a sandbox and shell-execution boundary, so automation should not choose the product/security semantics alone.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning plus docs/tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject explicit sandboxed PTY requests so callers cannot mistake pipe execution for a terminal session.

options.title: Support sandbox backend PTY
options.body: Pass PTY through to capable sandbox backends only after defining backend support, fallback behavior, docs, and tests.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning plus docs/tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the exec PTY contract and is the strongest history-backed owner for changing PTY semantics at the sandbox boundary.
